display.title: Tu B'Av: A Happy Day to Add in Torah Learning
display.summary_short: Why the fifteenth of Av is one of the happiest days for the Jewish people, and the custom to add more Torah learning from this day on.
display.summary_long: A short Tu B'Av talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. In the middle of the month of Av, a few days before the fifteenth, Uncle Yossi explains that the Mishnah says the Jewish people never had days as good as Chamishah Asar B'Av, because many happy things happened on it. Each year we remember those joyful events and pray that Hashem bring us days of joy again in our own time. Our Sages suggest a special custom for this day: to add more time to learning Torah, by day and especially at night, and to keep it up through the whole winter season. For soldiers in Tzivos Hashem, this means adding a little more to daily learning. Nothing is dearer to Hashem than seeing a child learn His Torah, and when Hashem is happy He blesses us with everything good for body and soul. It is also a great mitzvah to help a friend learn more, because whatever is good for you is good for your friend too.
display.lesson: From Tu B'Av on, add a little more Torah learning every day, especially at night, and encourage your friends to do the same.

date.note: 'This Friday will be Chamishah Asar B'Av' (Fri 26 Jul 1991); aired in episode 489, a Tuesday.

From the fifteenth of Av, add to Torah study at night; cited as what the Chachamim suggest.
